top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Helsinki Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
Helsinki Gran Fondo's urban rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
At mile 60 of 93, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at Helsinki Gran Fondo. Practice on urban: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 93 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Helsinki Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
At Helsinki Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
When someone attacks on urban, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Helsinki Gran Fondo's urban actually does to you.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 93 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Varied gradients on urban demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
2-minute all-out efforts on urban. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Helsinki Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Helsinki Gran Fondo’s 93 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, TT Threshold, and Durability to prepare you for 93 miles of urban in Helsinki Velodrome, Helsinki, Finland.
